summary: Octomancer's gift creates one 8/8 blue Octopus, independently of the article's count.
evidence: The allowed original Oracle reminder explicitly defines an 8/8 blue Octopus. CR702.174i defines the same intrinsic gift effect: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf . The pinned lowering and its mined template instead reuse the article 'an' as both token amount and power/toughness, making a 1/1. Change only those two stat expressions from Constant(1) to Constant(8); retain one token, GiftedPlayer, Blue/Creature/Octopus, untapped entry and the separate end-step copy trigger. The shared grammar declares this closed gift definition, rather than inferring stats from a count word. This corrects AST operands, not schema or an equality normalization. See the gift simplification notes.

summary: Use AnnouncedX consistently for a spell-own casting value in its conditions and target distribution.
evidence: These 28 numeric operands on 21 allowed faces query Source.SpellX in the same Spell frame whose other amounts and filters use AnnouncedX for the identical chosen X. CR107.3a defines that casting choice; CR707.10 preserves it when a spell is copied. Normalize only this own-spell value, including its announcement/distribution; retain thresholds, comparisons, branches, player/object identities and result IDs. Independent abilities, costs, delayed/reflexive/replacement programs, CastX history, EventActivationX, explicit other objects and captured values are excluded from the frontend normalization. No global Source/holder alias or schema change. Original Oracle wording is unchanged. Official rules: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf . See docs/spell-x-thresholds.md.

summary: Measure a proved single activation exile receipt as that card, consistently with ordinary object properties.
evidence: The allowed original Oracle texts name the mana value of one exiled card (Ellie and Alan) or creature (Food Chain). Both activation costs have one direct Move-to-Exile component with one selection choosing Exactly(Constant(1)); their existing operands sum ManaValue over that same Activation/Performed/After receipt. A sum over this proved singleton is its one card property, with CurrentOrLastKnown information, as in the existing singleton transition-receipt lowering. Keep the exact payment component, receipt phase, property, and all other operands; no zone query or persistent exiled-with alias is introduced. The frontend extends the existing singleton-receipt proof and reversible surface projection to these exact cost components. Other payment kinds, phases, views, plural or optional selections, malformed inputs and independent ability scopes are excluded. See docs/copiable-abilities-and-actions.md and src/bind/single_receipts.rs.

summary: Use the immediate whole-hand observation for card choices that query the same revealed hand.
evidence: These 79 operands on 78 allowed faces choose cards immediately after revealing that same complete hand. The old records query its current hand; other records and the shared observation grammar select from the revealed receipt, guarded by Hand and that same owner. With no intervening instruction or scope change, these represent the same population. Normalize only adjacent native Reveal(Zone Players Hand, Card, Any) followed by ChooseObjects from the identical one-player Hand/Card zone. Keep eligibility, count, chooser, selected/discard/exile receipts and other instructions. CR400.3 assigns hand cards to their owner; https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf . The owned bounded canonicalizer proves the same identity and preserves origin annotations, invalid fields and duplicate definitions; partial observations, other hands, intervening actions and independent frames do not acquire that receipt. See docs/nonlegendary-and-observed-hands.md.

summary: Represent a plain distinct exchange pair as one two-object target group.
evidence: Six plain Spell frames on four allowed faces exchange two permanents with identical target-free eligibility. Their old representation uses two required singleton slots, with an explicit Not(SameObject(first target)) on the second. This selects exactly the same distinct pair as one Exactly(2) target group. Preserve the first object at index 0 and map the second object to index 1; preserve the full eligibility, action, actor and surrounding abilities. Only a single ExchangeControl action, ordinary battlefield object domains and empty target metadata qualify. Different/target-dependent filters, optional counts, constraints, modal announcements and other instructions do not establish this proof. The owned typed, bounded normalizer validates lossless native input, keeps independent Spell/Spree scopes separate and carries coalesced declaration and operand origins. This is a semantic normal form change with no wire schema change. CR115.3: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf . See docs/copy-exceptions-and-exchange-pairs.md.
